title: Donde fue el árbol
desc: An address that names a tree cut down in 1998
setting: You have an address written on a piece of paper and it mentions no street at all.

options.es: Sí, señora. Busco esta dirección: de la iglesia, dos cuadras al lago.
options.en: Yes, madam. I am looking for this address: from the church, two blocks towards the lake.
options.feedback: You read her the address as it is written. Landmark, number of blocks, direction — that is the whole system.
She will help you anyway, but she needs the paper read out before she can.
You are standing on a corner turning a piece of paper around. She asked because it was obvious.

steps.speaker: Señora
steps.es: Ah, sí. Del árbol de mango, una cuadra abajo.
steps.en: Ah, yes. From the mango tree, one block down.

options.es: ¿Y dónde está el árbol de mango?
options.en: And where is the mango tree?
options.feedback: Ask, because you will not find it. Half the landmarks in Managua are things that are no longer there.
You have half an address. The half you are missing is the one that matters.

options.en: I do not see any tree.
options.feedback: Correct, and it sounds like you are telling her she is wrong. She is not.

steps.speaker: Señora
steps.es: El árbol ya no está, pero ahí fue. Todos saben.
steps.en: The tree is not there any more, but that is where it was. Everybody knows.

options.es: Ya. Entonces una cuadra abajo de donde estaba el árbol.
options.en: Right. So one block down from where the tree was.
options.feedback: You said it back in the past tense, which is exactly how Nicaraguans say these. Donde fue and donde estaba are addresses.
Probably. Repeating a landmark out loud is what stops you losing it at the next corner.

options.es: ¿Y cómo lo voy a saber yo?
options.en: And how am I supposed to know that?
options.feedback: Fair, and useless. Everybody in the barrio does know, and by next year you will too.

steps.speaker: Señora
steps.es: Eso. Y al lago es para el norte, ¿oyó?
steps.en: That is it. And towards the lake is north, all right?

options.es: Al lago es al norte y arriba es al este. Gracias, señora.
options.en: Towards the lake is north and up is east. Thank you, madam.
options.feedback: Four words that replace a map: al lago, al sur, arriba, abajo. Learn them once and the whole city opens.
Polite. She was giving you the compass, and it was worth repeating.
She just told you: the lake. In Managua the lake is always north and you can see where it is.
